question: What term describes the physical need for higher doses of a drug to get the same effect?
explanation: Tolerance happens when the body gets used to a drug, requiring larger amounts to produce the original feeling. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is addiction considered a chronic brain disease instead of just a lack of willpower?

options.A: It permanently alters brain circuits related to reward and self-control
options.B: It only affects people with inherited genetic weaknesses in their lungs
options.C: It completely stops the liver from producing digestive enzymes
options.D: It causes immediate physical paralysis in every single user

explanation: Think of it this way: long-term substance use physically changes how the brain's wiring works, making self-control super difficult without proper support. It's a health condition, not a character flaw! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are healthcare workers sometimes at higher risk for developing substance use issues?

options.A: They are completely exempt from the legal penalties of drug abuse
options.B: They experience heavy job stress and have easy access to medications
options.C: They receive special training on how to safely consume illegal substances
options.D: They possess a genetic immunity that makes them careless with drugs

explanation: The intense stress of clinical life combined with being around drugs all day creates a tough environment. Looking out for our mental health as nurses is so important! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical workplace stressor that puts nurses at risk?

options.A: Fatigue from rotating shift work disrupting normal sleep patterns
options.B: Chronic understaffing and heavy patient dependency loads
options.C: Exposure to traumatic patient deaths and emergency situations
options.D: Guaranteed 40-hour work weeks with zero night shifts

explanation: Predictable shifts with regular hours wouldn't cause the extreme burnout and exhaustion linked to nurse fatigue. If only every ward schedule was this nice! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention programs in substance abuse control?

options.A: Stopping individuals from ever experimenting with harmful drugs in the first place
options.B: Helping long-term recovering addicts find stable employment after treatment
options.C: Imposing strict criminal prison sentences on local drug traffickers
options.D: Providing immediate emergency detox in a specialized intensive care unit

explanation: Primary prevention is all about stopping the issue before it starts by educating healthy populations. Prevention is always better than cure! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why do pure scare tactics usually fail in teenage drug education programs?

options.A: Adolescents lack the physical ability to listen to spoken English instructions
options.B: Teens may find the exaggerated warnings do not match their real-world observations
options.C: Young people prefer reading detailed legal textbooks over listening to talks
options.D: Scare tactics automatically cure physical tolerance within twenty-four hours

explanation: When young people see friends using substances without immediate disaster, over-the-top scare stories lose all credibility. Honest, factual education works best! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using screening tools like CAGE or ASSIST in nursing?

options.A: To identify substance use problems early before they become severe
options.B: To gather legal evidence for immediate arrest by police officers
options.C: To test the chemical purity of substances seized on the street
options.D: To calculate the exact financial cost of a patient's drug habit

explanation: These quick screening tools help us spot risky habits early so we can step in with support before things get out of hand. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient gets defensive and stops answering when asked about alcohol intake. What should you do first as a nurse?

options.A: Immediately discharge the patient from the ward without further care
options.B: Reassure the patient of confidentiality and use a calm, non-judgmental tone
options.C: Document in bold red ink that the patient is a violent criminal
options.D: Threaten to report the patient to the hospital management and security

explanation: Building a safe space of trust and zero judgment is key to helping patients lower their guard and share the truth about their health. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of medical detoxification at the start of addiction treatment?

options.A: To safely manage acute physical withdrawal symptoms and stabilize the patient
options.B: To permanently cure the psychological craving for drugs within three days
options.C: To punish the patient so they never use illegal substances again
options.D: To teach vocational skills required for getting a job after discharge

explanation: Medical detox focuses on flushing the substance safely out of the body while keeping the patient comfortable through tough withdrawal symptoms. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) help someone recovering from substance use?

options.A: By forcing them to forget all memories of their friends and family
options.B: By curing any physical infections caused by dirty needles
options.C: By helping them recognize personal triggers and build healthy coping mechanisms
options.D: By replacing their natural blood chemistry with artificial synthetic hormones

explanation: CBT is fantastic because it trains the mind to spot what triggers cravings and teaches healthier ways to handle life's stress. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h5)

question: How should a healthcare team view a patient who relapses after months of being sober?

options.A: As a signal to review and adjust the treatment plan rather than a total failure
options.B: As an intentional crime that requires immediate notification of law enforcement
options.C: As an expected physical cure that means treatment is permanently finished
options.D: As definitive proof that the person is hopeless and should be abandoned

explanation: Just like managing hypertension or diabetes, a setback in a chronic condition means we tweak our approach, not give up on the patient! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a key part of long-term recovery support outside the hospital?

options.A: Total isolation from all human contact for the rest of one's life
options.B: Complete denial of employment opportunities until age sixty
options.C: Daily mandatory drug infusions supervised by armed security guards
options.D: Participation in peer support groups and ongoing community aftercare

explanation: Staying connected to a supportive community and peer groups makes a huge difference in maintaining long-term recovery. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency handles drug law enforcement, arresting traffickers, and seizing illegal substances?
explanation: The NDLEA is Nigeria's main federal body tasked with tackling drug trafficking and enforcing drug control laws. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is a major public health downside of relying solely on harsh criminal punishment for substance abuse?

options.A: It automatically cures physical dependence within forty-eight hours
options.B: It forces pharmaceutical companies to stop manufacturing all antibiotics
options.C: It drives vulnerable drug users underground and prevents them from seeking medical help
options.D: It eliminates every single illegal drug farm in the entire world

explanation: When people fear police arrest and prison, they tend to stay away from hospitals during overdoses or medical crises, which puts lives at risk. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h7)

question: What personal quality is essential for a nurse caring for patients with substance use disorders?

options.A: Willingness to lecture and scold patients about their past mistakes
options.B: Strict refusal to administer any form of pain relief medication
options.C: Belief that addiction is simply a moral failing and personal choice
options.D: Self-awareness to recognize and manage personal biases against addiction

explanation: To give truly professional care, we must check our personal judgments at the door and treat every patient with empathy. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h8)

question: You notice a fellow nurse showing signs of severe impairment while on duty. What is the best professional step to take?

options.A: Keep the secret permanently and let the impaired nurse handle critical drug doses alone
options.B: Report the observation safely through institutional channels to protect patients and help the colleague
options.C: Steal some of the leftover medications for personal use after the shift ends
options.D: Shout insults at the colleague in front of patients and visitors in the hallway

explanation: Patient safety always comes first, but we also want to guide our struggling colleagues toward the help they need through proper, confidential channels. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h8)
